mcqs.question: Which of the following objects is the poorest reflector of light?
mcqs.explanation: A black matte board absorbs most of the incident light and reflects very little, making it a poor reflecting surface. Polished metal, white paper, and water all reflect a noticeable amount of light. Hence option C is correct.

mcqs.question: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror at an angle of 30° to the normal. What is the angle of reflection measured from the normal?
mcqs.explanation: For a plane (smooth) surface, the law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Since the incidence angle is 30°, the reflected angle is also 30°. Therefore option A is correct.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes regular reflection from irregular reflection?

options.A: Regular reflection occurs on smooth surfaces producing a single reflected ray; irregular reflection occurs on rough surfaces producing many scattered rays.
options.B: Regular reflection occurs on rough surfaces producing many scattered rays; irregular reflection occurs on smooth surfaces producing a single reflected ray.
options.C: Both regular and irregular reflection always produce a single reflected ray.
options.D: Both regular and irregular reflection always produce many scattered rays.

mcqs.answer: Regular reflection occurs on smooth surfaces producing a single reflected ray; irregular reflection occurs on rough surfaces producing many scattered rays.
mcqs.explanation: A smooth (polished) surface reflects light in a single, well‑defined direction – this is regular (specular) reflection. A rough surface reflects light in many directions, giving irregular (diffuse) reflection. Option A captures this distinction correctly.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate reflection to mirrors and everyday applications
mcqs.question: A periscope used by submarines works on the principle of reflection. Which arrangement of mirrors inside the periscope makes this possible?

options.A: Two plane mirrors placed parallel to each other
options.B: Two plane mirrors placed at right angles to each other
options.C: A concave mirror followed by a convex mirror

mcqs.answer: Two plane mirrors placed at right angles to each other
mcqs.explanation: A periscope contains two plane mirrors positioned at 45° to the line of sight, i.e., at right angles to each other. This arrangement reflects light down the tube and then out to the viewer’s eye, allowing observation from a concealed position. Options A, C, and D do not produce the required change in direction.

mcqs.question: What is meant by the reflection of light?

options.A: The bouncing back of light from a surface
options.B: The bending of light when it passes from one medium to another
options.C: The splitting of white light into its component colours
options.D: The absorption of light by a surface

mcqs.answer: The bouncing back of light from a surface
mcqs.explanation: Reflection is the process where light rays strike a surface and bounce back into the same medium. Bending of light is refraction, splitting into colours is dispersion, and absorption is when light energy is taken up by the material.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a good reflecting surface for visible light?
mcqs.explanation: Polished metal has a smooth, shiny surface that reflects most of the incident light. Transparent glass allows light to pass through, sandpaper scatters light (irregular reflection), and black cloth absorbs light, making them poor reflectors.

mcqs.question: When light reflects from a plane surface, which statement is true?

options.A: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal.
options.B: The angle of incidence is always larger than the angle of reflection.
options.C: The reflected ray always passes through the point of incidence.
options.D: The reflected ray travels inside the material.

mcqs.answer: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal.
mcqs.explanation: The law of reflection for a plane (smooth) surface states that the incident angle and reflected angle are equal when measured with respect to the normal line at the point of incidence. Options B, C, and D are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following situations demonstrates irregular (diffuse) reflection?

options.A: A calm lake reflecting the sky
options.D: A smooth water surface in a swimming pool

mcqs.explanation: Frosted glass has a rough surface that scatters incident light in many directions, producing irregular (diffuse) reflection. The lake, polished mirror, and smooth water surface all produce regular (specular) reflection.
